claims.claim: Photius I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 858 to 867 and from 877 to 886.
Photius was born circa 815 and died on 6 February 893.
Photius was recognized in the Eastern Orthodox Church as 'Saint Photius the Great'.
Photius was a leading figure of the 9th-century Byzantine renascence.
Photius was born in Constantinople to a noble family.
Photius was related through his father to Tarasius, who was patriarch from 784 to 806.
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Ephesios is part of a larger collection of Photius's fragmentary commentaries on the Pauline epistles.
